book.new: {t('Every white key has a name, a letter from A to G. Each house from Chapter 2 now gets its names. Then the names get fast: forwards, backwards, in skips, all over the piano. book.old: <>음악은 알파벳 처음 일곱 글자만 써요: A B C D E F G. 피아노 맨 아래 건반이 바로 A예요. 거기서부터 흰건반을 하나씩 올라가며 알파벳 순서대로: A B C D E F G, 그리고 다시 A. 집이 자리를 알려 줘요: C D E는 작은 집에, F G A B는 큰 집에 살아요. C와 F는 각 집의 왼쪽 문이에요. (도레미로는 C가 도, D가 레, E가 미...)
book.new: <>음악은 알파벳 처음 일곱 글자만 써요: A B C D E F G. 맨 아래 건반이 A예요. 거기서부터 흰건반이 A부터 G까지 올라가고, 그다음 다시 A예요. C D E는 작은 집에, F G A B는 큰 집에 살아요. C와 F는 왼쪽 문이에요. 도레미로는 C가 도, D가 레, E가 미...

book.old: <>Music uses just the first seven letters of the alphabet: A B C D E F G. The very lowest key on the piano is an A. From there, the white keys go up in alphabet order: A B C D E F G, and then A again. The houses tell you where each one lives: C D E in the small house, F G A B in the big one, with C and F at the left doors. (In Do Re Mi, C is Do, D is Re, E is Mi...)
book.new: <>Music uses only the first seven letters of the alphabet: A B C D E F G. The lowest key is an A. From there the white keys go up A to G, then A again. C D E live in the small house, F G A B in the big house. C and F are the left doors. In Do Re Mi, C is Do, D is Re, E is Mi...

book.old: <>누가 글자를 하나 말하면, 집을 보고 그 건반을 찾아요. 세 군데에서 쳐 봐요.</>
book.new: <>누가 글자를 말하면, 집을 보고 찾아요. 세 군데에서 쳐 봐요.</>

book.old: <>Someone says a letter; use the houses to find it. Then play it in three different places.</>
book.new: <>Someone says a letter; find it by its house. Play it in three places.</>

book.old: <>음악에는 글자 일곱 개만 있어요: A B C D E F G. G 다음엔 관람차가 돌아 다시 A가 와요: 요일처럼 돌고 돌아요, H는 없어요. 한 바퀴 돌 때마다 같은 글자가 다시 와요. C에서 다음 C까지를 옥타브라고 해요. '옥트(oct)'는 8이라는 뜻, 문어(octopus)의 다리 여덟 개처럼요: 두 C를 모두 세면 흰건반 8개. 이름은 같고, 목소리만 더 높아요.
book.new: <>일곱 글자는 관람차처럼 돌고 돌아요. G 다음엔 다시 A, 요일처럼요. H는 없어요. C에서 다음 C까지가 옥타브예요: 두 C를 모두 세면 흰건반 8개. '옥트(oct)'는 8, 문어(octopus)의 다리 여덟 개처럼요. 이름은 같고, 목소리만 더 높아요.

book.old: <>Music uses only seven letters: A B C D E F G. After G, the wheel comes round to A again: round and round like the days of the week; there is no H. Each time round, the same letter comes back. From one C up to the next C is called an octave. oct means eight, like the eight legs of an octopus: 8 white keys, counting both Cs. Same name, higher voice.
book.new: <>The seven letters go round and round like a wheel. After G comes A again, like the days of the week. There is no H. From one C to the next is an octave: 8 white keys, counting both Cs. oct means eight, like an octopus's eight legs. Same name, higher voice.

book.old: <>가운데 도에서 흰건반 8개를 걸어 올라가 다음 C까지 가요. 한 옥타브, 관람차가 한 바퀴 돌았어요.
book.new: <>가운데 도에서 다음 C까지 흰건반 8개를 글자를 말하며 올라가요. 한 옥타브, 관람차 한 바퀴.

book.old: <>Play middle C, then walk up 8 white keys to the next C, saying the letters. One octave: the wheel has gone round once.
book.new: <>From middle C, walk up 8 white keys to the next C, saying the letters. One octave, one turn of the wheel.

book.old: <>피아노를 위로(오른쪽, 하늘 위 새 쪽으로) 올라가면 글자는 앞으로 가요: C D E F G A B C. 아래로(왼쪽, 바다 아래 거북이 쪽으로) 내려가면 관람차가 거꾸로 돌고 글자도 거꾸로 가요: C B A G F E D C. 거꾸로가 어려워요: 건반 위에서도, 머릿속으로도, 앞으로만큼 빨리 나올 때까지 말해 봐요.
book.new: <>위로(오른쪽, 하늘의 새 쪽) 가면 글자는 앞으로 가요: C D E F G A B C. 아래로(왼쪽, 바다의 거북이 쪽) 가면 관람차가 거꾸로 돌고 글자도 거꾸로 가요: C B A G F E D C. 거꾸로가 더 어려워요: 건반에서도, 머릿속으로도 연습해요.

book.old: <>Going up the piano, to the right, towards the bird in the sky, the letters go forwards: C D E F G A B C. Going down, to the left, towards the turtle under the sea, the wheel turns the other way, and the letters go backwards: C B A G F E D C. Backwards is the tricky one: say it until it comes as quickly as forwards, on the keys, and in your head.
book.new: <>Going up (right, to the bird's sky), the letters go forwards: C D E F G A B C. Going down (left, to the turtle's sea), the wheel turns back and they go backwards: C B A G F E D C. Backwards is harder: practise it on the keys and in your head.

book.old: <>Start on G and go down to the G below. Careful where the wheel turns back from A to G!
book.new: <>From G, go down to the G below. Careful at the turn from A to G!

book.old: <>피아노도 건반도 없이: 머릿속으로 거꾸로 말해요(G F E D C B A). 그다음 E에서, B에서, 아무 글자에서나 시작해요.
book.new: <>머릿속으로 거꾸로 말해요: G F E D C B A. 그다음 E에서, B에서, 아무 글자에서나 시작해요.

book.old: <>No piano, no keys: say the letters backwards in your head (G F E D C B A). Then start from E, from B, from any letter.
book.new: <>Say the letters backwards in your head: G F E D C B A. Then start from E, from B, from any letter.

book.old: <>매번 C부터 걸어가면 느려요. 대신 누가 사는지 봐요. 작은 집에는 왼쪽 문에 꼬마 공주 클라라(Clara), C가 살고, 검은건반 두 개 사이 개집에는 클라라의 강아지(Dog), D가 살아요. 오른쪽 문은 출구(Exit), E예요. 큰 집에는 앞문(Front door) F와 뒷문(Back door) B가 있고, 그 안에는 사과를 좋아하는 할머니(Grandma) G가 살아요. 그래서 바로 옆이 할머니의 사과 정원(Apple garden), A예요.
book.new: <>매번 C부터 걸어가면 느려요. 누가 사는지 봐요. C: 작은 집 왼쪽 문의 꼬마 공주 클라라(Clara). D: 검은건반 두 개 사이 개집에 사는 클라라의 강아지(Dog). E: 오른쪽 문, 출구(Exit). F: 큰 집의 앞문(Front door). G: 안에 사는, 사과를 좋아하는 할머니(Grandma). A: 바로 옆, 할머니의 사과 정원(Apple garden). B: 뒷문(Back door).

book.old: <>Walking up from C every time is slow. Instead, look at who lives there. In the small house lives Clara, a little princess, at the left door (C), with her Dog in his doghouse between the two black keys (D); the right door is the Exit (E). The big house has a Front door (F) and a Back door (B); inside lives Grandma (G), who loves apples. So right next to her is her Apple garden (A).
book.new: <>Walking up from C every time is slow. Look at who lives there. C: Clara, a little princess, at the small house's left door. D: her Dog, in his doghouse between the two black keys. E: the Exit, the right door. F: the big house's Front door. G: Grandma, who lives inside and loves apples. A: her Apple garden, right next to her. B: the Back door.

book.old: <>한 걸음은 바로 다음 글자로 가요. 건너뛰기는 하나를 넘어가요: C, (D), E, (F), G... 관람차를 건너뛰며 한 바퀴 돌면(C E G B D F A, 그리고 다시 C) 선이 별을 그려요. 피아노에서 건너뛰기는 흰건반 하나를 넘어가는 거예요. 처음에는 넘어가는 글자를 속삭여요: C (d) E (f) G. 그다음 속삭임을 빼요.
book.new: <>한 걸음은 바로 다음 글자로 가요. 건너뛰기는 글자 하나, 흰건반 하나를 넘어가요: C, (D), E, (F), G... 관람차를 건너뛰며 한 바퀴 돌면(C E G B D F A, 다시 C) 선이 별을 그려요. 처음에는 넘어가는 글자를 속삭여요: C (d) E (f) G. 그다음 속삭임을 빼요.

book.old: <>A step goes to the very next letter. A skip jumps over one: C, (D), E, (F), G... Skip all the way round the wheel (C E G B D F A, and back to C) and the lines draw a star. On the piano, a skip jumps over one white key. At first, whisper the letter you jump over: C (d) E (f) G. Then leave the whisper out.
book.new: <>A step goes to the very next letter. A skip jumps over one letter, one white key: C, (D), E, (F), G... Skip round the wheel (C E G B D F A, back to C) and the lines draw a star. At first, whisper the skipped letter: C (d) E (f) G. Then drop the whisper.

book.old: <>이제 글자를 읽고 바로 쳐요. 오른손 2 3 4를 작은 집의 C D E에 올려요: 글자를 읽고, 자리를 보고, 쳐요. 이번에는 손가락 번호가 아니라 글자를 읽어요. 그다음 왼손으로, 작은 집 하나 아래에서 쳐 봐요.
book.new: <>오른손 2 3 4를 작은 집의 C D E에 올려요. 글자를 읽고, 자리를 보고, 쳐요. 손가락 번호가 아니라 글자를 읽어요. 그다음 왼손으로, 작은 집 하나 아래에서 쳐 봐요.

book.old: <>Now read the letters and play them. Right-hand 2 3 4 sit on C D E in the small house: read each letter, see its place, play. This time you read the letters, not the finger numbers. Then try the left hand, one small house lower.
book.new: <>Right-hand 2 3 4 sit on C D E in the small house. Read each letter, see its place, play. Read the letters, not the finger numbers. Then try the left hand, one small house lower.

book.old: <>Find the lowest key on the piano: it is A. Walk up the white keys saying A B C D E F G, and A again.
book.new: <>Find the lowest key, an A. Walk up the white keys saying A B C D E F G, and A again.

book.old: <>모든 C(작은 집의 왼쪽 문)와 모든 F(큰 집의 왼쪽 문)를 찾아 쳐요.
book.new: <>모든 C와 모든 F를 찾아 쳐요: 두 집의 왼쪽 문이에요.

book.old: <>Find and play every C (the small house's left door) and every F (the big house's left door).
book.new: <>Find and play every C and every F: the two houses' left doors.

guide.old: Every white key on the piano has a name: a letter from A to G, the first seven letters of the alphabet. Learn where each letter lives, then make the names come fast, until any key tells you its name at a glance.
guide.new: Every white key has a name: a letter from A to G. Learn where each one lives, then make the names fast, until any key tells you its name at a glance.

guide.old: Music uses just the first seven letters of the alphabet: A B C D E F G. The very lowest key on the piano is an A. From there, the white keys go up in alphabet order, A B C D E F G, and then A again.
guide.new: Music uses the first seven letters of the alphabet: A B C D E F G. The lowest key on the piano is an A. From there the white keys go up A to G, then A again.

guide.old: • C and F are the left doors of the two houses: find them first, and walk from there.
guide.new: • C and F are the two left doors. Find them first and walk from there.

guide.old: After G, the letters come round to A again, like the days of the week; there is no H. Each time round, the same letter comes back.
guide.new: After G comes A again, like the days of the week. There is no H.

guide.old: From one C up to the next C is called an octave: oct means eight, like the eight legs of an octopus, and an octave is 8 white keys, counting both Cs. Same name, higher voice.
guide.new: From one C to the next is an octave: 8 white keys, counting both Cs. oct means eight, like an octopus's eight legs. Same name, higher voice.

guide.old: Going up the piano, to the right, the letters go forwards: C D E F G A B C. Going down, to the left, they go backwards: C B A G F E D C. Backwards is the tricky one, especially the turn from A back to G.
guide.new: Going up (right), the letters go forwards: C D E F G A B C. Going down (left), they go backwards: C B A G F E D C. Backwards is harder, especially the turn from A to G.

guide.old: Walking up from C every time is slow. Instead, look at who lives there.
guide.new: Walking up from C every time is slow. Look at who lives there.

guide.old: In the small house lives Clara, a little princess, at the left door (C), with her Dog in his doghouse between the two black keys (D). The right door is the Exit (E).
guide.new: C: Clara, a little princess, at the small house's left door. D: her Dog, in his doghouse between the two black keys. E: the Exit, the right door.

guide.old: The big house has a Front door (F) and a Back door (B). Inside lives Grandma (G), who loves apples, so right next to her is her Apple garden (A).
guide.new: F: the big house's Front door. G: Grandma, who lives inside and loves apples. A: her Apple garden, right next to her. B: the Back door.

guide.old: Every word starts with its key's letter, and every one sits in its key's place in the house. Don't count from C: ask who lives there.
guide.new: Each name starts with its key's letter and sits in its key's place. Don't count from C: ask who lives there.

guide.old: A step goes to the very next letter. A skip jumps over one: C, (D), E, (F), G. Skip all the way round, C E G B D F A and back to C, and the lines draw a seven-pointed star. On the piano, a skip jumps over one white key.
guide.new: A step goes to the very next letter. A skip jumps over one letter, one white key: C, (D), E, (F), G. Skip round, C E G B D F A and back to C, and the lines draw a seven-pointed star.

guide.old: At first, whisper the letter you jump over, C (d) E (f) G, then leave the whisper out.
guide.new: At first, whisper the skipped letter, C (d) E (f) G. Then drop the whisper.

guide.old: Now the letters go straight onto the keys. Right-hand fingers 2, 3 and 4 sit on C, D and E in the small house: read each letter, see its place, play. This time the student reads the letters, not the finger numbers. Then the left hand, one small house lower.
guide.new: Right-hand fingers 2, 3 and 4 sit on C, D and E in the small house. Read each letter, see its place, play. Read the letters, not the finger numbers. Then the left hand, one small house lower.

guide.old: Spell and play: a word made only of music letters is a tiny tune. Try BAG, CAFE, FACE, BEAD and EGG, saying each letter as you play it.
guide.new: Spell and play: a word made only of music letters is a tiny tune. Try BAG, CAFE, FACE, BEAD and EGG, saying each letter.

guide.old: The white keys use the first seven letters of the alphabet, A B C D E F G. After G the letters start again at A, so the same seven names repeat all the way up the piano. There is no H.
guide.new: The white keys use the first seven letters of the alphabet: A B C D E F G. After G comes A again, so the seven names repeat all the way up the piano. There is no H.

guide.old: Use the black keys. C D E sit around the group of two black keys, F G A B around the group of three. C is just left of the two, F just left of the three, D sits between the two, and G and A sit between the three.
guide.new: Use the black keys. C D E sit around the two black keys, F G A B around the three. C is just left of the two, F just left of the three. D sits between the two, G and A between the three.

guide.old: The distance from one letter to the next key with the same name, for example from one C up to the next C. It spans 8 white keys, counting both ends: oct means eight.
guide.new: The distance from one key to the next key with the same letter, like C up to the next C: 8 white keys, counting both ends. oct means eight.
